title: Factors associated with deaf‑mutism in children attending special schools of rural central India: A survey
summary: background : the aim of this study was to determine the prevalence of hearing impairment among children in the rural areas of karnataka state , india.materials and methods : a cross - sectional study was carried out in all primary and secondary schools of rural area , karnataka state of india . <n> data were collected from the records of the schools selected by the random sampling method.results:a total of 2160 children were included in the study . the prevalence rate of hearing loss in children in rural area was 3.2% ( 95% ci : 2.0%-3.33% ) . in this study , there was no statistically significant difference in prevalence rate between urban and rural areas.conclusions:the study concluded that there is no significant difference between rural and urban areas with regard to hearing impairment .
key_findings: Prevalence of hearing loss in rural children is 3.2%
No significant difference in prevalence between urban and rural areas
Study included 2160 children from rural Karnataka
methodology: A cross-sectional study was conducted in primary and secondary schools of rural Karnataka, with data collected from school records using random sampling.
limitations: Study limited to rural areas of Karnataka
Data based on school records may not capture all cases
future_work: Investigate factors contributing to hearing impairment in urban settings
Conduct longitudinal studies to track hearing loss over time
Explore interventions to improve hearing health in rural populations
